title: WPMB/620/2026 of M/S ARIF ENTERPRISES Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE SHRI MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE SHRI SUBHASH UPADHYAY
13th August, 2026
WRIT PETITION (M/B) NO.620 of 2026
M/s Arif Enterprises ------Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and Others ----Respondents
Presence:-
Mr. Abhijay Negi, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Rahul Verma, learned Additional Advocate General for the
State.
Mr. S. C. Bhatt, learned counsel for the respondent no.3.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT: (per Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
1. The present writ petition has been filed challenging
the rejection of the petitioner's bid in the technical round on
ground of non-submission of the mandatory documents as well
as EMD and tender fee.
2. The petitioner is a company incorporated under the
Companies Act. It is stated to have submitted its bid for a
work pertaining to: collection and disposal waste management
service; collection, lifting, transportation, unloading,
segregation of garbage, sweeping as per RFP; dry waste. The
petitioner's bid has been rejected in technical round on the
grounds aforesaid.
3. The petitioner has assailed the decision of the
Technical Committee rejecting its technical bid contending that
the petitioner is registered as an MSME, therefore, in terms of
the Public Procurement Policy notified by the State

2026:UHC:7209-DB
Government dated 28.08.2019, it is exempted from payment
of tender fee and Earnest Money Deposit (EMD). It is
submitted that consequently, the decision of the Technical
Evaluation Committee rejecting the technical bid of the
petitioner is not sustainable in law. It is further submitted that
the petitioner was not given any time by the Technical
Evaluation Committee to remove the defects in the technical
bid or to supply the missing documents, and this according to
the petitioner, has also rendered illegal the decision of the
Technical Committee.
4. Respondent no.3 has filed a counter affidavit,
wherein the stand taken is that apart from not submitting EMD
and tender fee, the petitioner had also not submitted the
required mandatory documents, consequently, the bid had
been rightly rejected. A copy of the tabular chart prepared by
the Technical Evaluation Committee listing therein the details
of the documents submitted/ not submitted by each tenderer
has been annexed. It reveals that the petitioner, apart from
not submitting EMD and tender fee, had also not submitted
Power of Attorney, Certificate of Incorporation, PAN card,
audited financial statements, CA Certificate for turnover,
similar experience years certificate, completion certificate,
manpower deployment format, vehicle deployment format. A
perusal of annexure no.3, which is RFP, reveals that various
certificates were to be submitted in prescribed format and they
2

were part of RFP. Annexure no.8 to the RFP is manpower
deployment format, which was not submitted; annexure no.9
to RFP is vehicle deployment format, which was also not
submitted; annexure no.20 to RFP is checklist of documents,
which was also not submitted. Moreover, it is not disputed that
submission of PAN and other documents was also essential
conditions of the RFP.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner does not dispute
that the aforesaid documents were not submitted by the
petitioner along with its technical bid. Consequently, even if we
accept the contention that the petitioner being MSME was not
required to submit tender fee and EMD, the non-filing of other
mandatory documents rightly resulted in disqualification of the
petitioner in the technical round. Therefore, we find no merit
in the writ petition and the same is dismissed.
6. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of
accordingly.

(MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C.J.)
 (SUBHASH UPADHYAY, J.)
